question: According to the 2011 census of India, the literacy rate in India is ____ percent.
solution:
The correct answer is __**74.04**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The literacy rate in India as per the 2011 census is **74.04%**.
 
• The literacy rate is an important indicator of a country's educational development and human resource quality.
 
• The census is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• The 2011 census was the 15th National Census of the country since 1872.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Literacy Rate**

 
 
• The literacy rate is defined as the percentage of people who are able to read and write with understanding, among the population aged 7 years and above.
 
• A higher literacy rate indicates better educational opportunities and improved socio-economic conditions.
 
• In 2001, the literacy rate in India was 64.8%, showing a significant improvement in 2011.
 
• Factors affecting literacy rates include access to education, quality of education, government policies, socio-economic conditions, and cultural attitudes towards education.
 
 
 
• **Census**
 
 
• The Census of India is one of the largest administrative exercises in the world, aiming to capture detailed information about the population.
 
• The first synchronous census in India was held in 1881, and it has been conducted every decade since then.
 
• The census collects data on various parameters such as population size, demographics, economic activity, literacy, housing, and amenities.
 
• Data from the census is crucial for planning, policy-making, and administration at various levels of government.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Literacy**
 
 
• Literacy is a key component of human development, enabling individuals to access information, improve their socio-economic status, and participate fully in society.
 
• It has a direct impact on health, employment, and income levels, contributing to overall national development.
 
• Efforts to improve literacy rates include government initiatives such as the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Mid-Day Meal Scheme, and National Literacy Mission.
 
• Non-governmental organizations and community-based programs also play a significant role in promoting literacy.
